title: Microsoft Dataverse: run prompt columns on existing records in bulk (backfill)
summary: The briefing's availability, licensing, defaults, job limits and controls are supported by the roadmap record and Microsoft Learn. Microsoft's two administration pages differ on the heading above the AI prompts switch; the briefing should acknowledge that navigation discrepancy.

claims.claim: Dataverse prompt columns can generate values for existing records in bulk, rather than only new or updated records.
claims.quote: Prompt columns can now generate AI values for records that already exist in your table, not just new or updated ones.

claims.claim: Makers can optionally filter the existing records to which a bulk prompt applies.
claims.quote: Makers can choose to apply a prompt to existing records in bulk, optionally filtered to just the rows they need

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: Backfill is admin-opt-in: an administrator must enable the environment setting before makers can use the bulk option.
claims.quote: Allow bulk processing of existing records: This setting is off by default. Turn it on to run the prompt on existing records in bulk in an environment.

claims.claim: The bulk setting is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Allow bulk processing of existing records.
claims.quote: Two environment settings in the Power Platform admin center control this option. Select your environment and go to Settings > Features. ... Allow bulk processing of existing records

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an API or automation call for the Allow bulk processing of existing records switch.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse "Allow bulk processing of existing records" API organization; "prompt column" "bulk" "API" settings. Read prompt-column, settings-features and Organization reference; searched Organization for bulk/prompt/import/review. No matching setting operation found.

claims.claim: Allow bulk processing of existing records is off by default.

claims.claim: Updating settings in Features requires the System Administrator security role or equivalent permissions.

claims.quote: Select your environment and go to Settings > Features. ... Require review before processing imported prompt columns: This setting is on by default.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an API or automation call for the Require review before processing imported prompt columns switch.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The enabled import-review setting pauses an imported job in System jobs until it is manually started after review.
claims.quote: It controls the job's behavior on solution import in an environment. When enabled, an imported job pauses for review in System jobs and can be manually started after review.

claims.claim: The Specialized columns using code page still says importing and exporting solutions with prompt columns is unsupported.
claims.quote: Importing and exporting solutions with prompt columns is not supported at this time.

claims.quote: Select Environments > [select an environment] > Settings > Product > Features. ... On the Features settings page under AI Builder, enable or disable the AI prompts toggle.

claims.claim: Learn documents backfill under Apply prompt to existing records in bulk.
claims.quote: Apply prompt to existing records in bulk ... Use this option to run the prompt for existing records in bulk (backfill).

claims.claim: Makers access the bulk option by opening their prompt column from Tables in Power Apps.
claims.quote: Go to Power Apps, select Tables on the left navigation pane, and open your prompt column.

claims.claim: The maker selects Also generate values for Existing records in bulk on the column panel.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The maker is shown the number of records and estimated credit consumption before saving and running the backfill.
claims.quote: Review the number of records to process and the estimated credit consumption for the job, and save the column configuration.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: After saving the column configuration, the maker selects Run prompt to queue the job.
claims.quote: Save the column configuration. ... Select Run prompt when you're ready to queue the job.

claims.claim: Backfill generates values through an asynchronous background job managed in System jobs.
claims.quote: When you select this option, the system generates the values as an asynchronous background job managed in System jobs.

claims.claim: The system updates the prompt column and its Status and Details columns as each record completes.
claims.quote: The system updates the prompt column, along with its Status and Details columns, as each record completes.

claims.claim: Creating a record triggers the prompt.
claims.quote: A prompt executes when you create a record or update one or more of the columns that the prompt references.

claims.claim: Updating one or more columns referenced by the prompt triggers execution.
claims.quote: A prompt executes when you create a record or update one or more of the columns that the prompt references.

claims.claim: Microsoft's FAQ says updating a prompt definition does not recalculate existing values until a later update to a referenced column.
claims.quote: Updating the prompt definition does not recalculate existing prompt values until a subsequent update occurs on one or more columns defined in the prompt.

claims.claim: The pre-backfill behavior did not automatically populate a newly added prompt column for existing records.
claims.quote: When prompt columns are added to tables with records, the existing records' new prompt columns aren't populated automatically.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Each prompt execution in the backfill consumes credits.
claims.quote: Prompt columns consume credits every time a prompt is executed.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing: Capacity
claims.claim: Microsoft tells administrators to ensure sufficient AI credit capacity in the environment before enabling bulk processing.
claims.quote: Ensure sufficient AI credit capacity is available in the environment before enabling it.

claims.claim: A prompt column passes its input-column data to an AI model for generation.
claims.quote: The AI model processes these prompts to generate relevant responses based on specified input columns.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Generated prompt-column values persist in the table containing the source data.
claims.quote: Natural language prompts tied to other columns in your table. ... The key function is that the prompt column contains generative AI results stored in the table persistently.

claims.claim: Microsoft's prompts overview says prompts use models powered by Azure Foundry.
claims.quote: Prompts use models powered by Azure Foundry.

claims.claim: Users able to read a prompt output column can see its generated data, including information derived from secured input columns unless the output is secured too.
claims.quote: When a calculated column or prompt column includes a column that is secured, data might be displayed in the calculated or prompt column to users that don't have permission to the secured column. Both the original column and the calculated or prompt column should be secured.

claims.claim: Microsoft lists insufficient user permissions on an input column as a cause of prompt-column execution failure.
claims.quote: The user doesn't have sufficient permissions on one or more input columns referenced in the prompt column definition.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends human review of generated content before using it to inform a business decision.
